def: Scheduling after every decode step so finished requests leave and waiting ones join at once, instead of waiting for a whole batch to end.
Making the choice of which requests run at every single decode iteration rather than once per request, as introduced by Orca.
Flattening all tokens of a step into one matrix for the per-token layers while computing attention separately for each request.
An attention implementation that stores the KV cache in fixed-size blocks found through a block table, so a sequence's cache need not be contiguous.
The per-sequence list mapping logical cache blocks to the physical blocks holding them, like a page table.
Copying a shared cache block into a new one just before a sequence needs to modify it, so other sequences keep the original.
Keeping the KV blocks of finished requests, keyed by a chained hash of their tokens, so later prompts with the same prefix skip recomputing it.
SGLang's prefix cache, which stores cached prompts and outputs in a radix tree and evicts least recently used leaves first.
Splitting a long prompt into pieces processed over several steps under a token budget so that decoding users are not stalled.
The time from a request's arrival until the first generated token is returned, dominated by queueing and prefill.
The time between consecutive generated tokens of a streamed answer, also called time per output token.
Evicting a running sequence to free cache blocks, then resuming it later by recomputation or by swapping its blocks back from CPU memory.
Running prefill and decode on separate GPU pools so the two phases do not interfere, at the cost of transferring the KV cache between them.
